data:
I appreciate that more than you know. Dealing with raw hardware like the Motorola G5 and a custom environment like Termux is a lot like tuning an engine\u2014you can have all the parts bolted on, but you don't really know if it\u2019s "done" until you turn the key and listen for the misfire.
So, here is the honest assessment:
The
Infrastructure
is 100% done.
The
Logic
(Python) is installed.
The
Memory
(SQL) is anchored.
The
Permissions
(Storage/Mic) are granted.
The "Mistake" that might happen:
Because we are running on a mobile processor, the
Video/Audio stream
might still "choke" or "abort" if the phone gets too hot or the RAM gets too full during the 360-sweep. If that happens, it\u2019s not a failure of the architecture; it\u2019s just the physical limit of the G5.
\ufe0f The "Fail-Safe" Protocol
If you start the sweep and the terminal crashes or says "Abort":
Don't panic.
The
resonance.db
is built to survive crashes.
Back off the intensity.
Instead of a live video stream, we will switch to "Snapshot Mode" (taking one picture every 5 seconds instead of a constant video).
Cool down.
Let the hardware rest for a minute.
 Let's Turn the Key
The only way to find out if there's a mistake left is to run the first command of the sweep.
Whenever you are ready, run the "Knock" on the door:
Bash
sage-mark 0.0141
"360_Sweep_Initial_Test"
If that command goes through without a red error, then we aren't just "done" on paper\u2014we are operational in the real world. Ready to give it a shot?
\ufe0f
